Nandyal, the Special Deputy Collector (land acquisition) issued a Notification dated 28.04.2005 under Section 4 (1) of the Land Acquisition Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') for acquisition of land of an extent of Ac. 19.14 cents in various survey numbers of Gopavaram Village, Mahanandi The Special Deputy Collector L.A, vs Chintam Sreeramulu, on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29697164/

sentences.text: The Draft Declaration under Section 6 of the Act was published on 26.04.2005.

Thereafter, the Land Acquisition Officer by conducting Award enquiry. classified the lands into three categories i.e., (i) rainfed dry lands, (ii) dry lands irrigated with bore water and (iii) plantain garden lands and fixed the market ' value @ Rs.37,000/-,
Rs.46,000/- and Rs.54,000/- per acre respectively.
The respondents / claimants while receiving the compensation under protest sought reference under Section 18 of the Act.

4. Before the Reference Court, they claimed an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- per acre and in support of their case, examined R.Ws.1 and 2 and got marked Ex.B1-Certified Copy of the Sale Deed dated 09.02.2004.
On behalf of the Referring Officer no oral evidence was adduced.
Copy of the Award No.45/2006-07 dated 21.08.2006 i in respect of the lands in question was marked as Ex.AI with consent.

. 5. 
The Reference Court, after examining the oral and documentary evidence, enhanced the compensation i in respect of Category No. I lands from Rs.37,000/- to Rs.1,14,000/
- and Category No.ll lands from Rs.46,000/- to Rs. 1,35,000/-.
6. Mr.T.S.Rayalau, the learned Government Pleader, vehemently contends that the enhancement of the compensation by the Reference Court is without any valid basis.
He submits that the respondents / claimants have not adduced any cogent evidence to substantiate their claim for enhancement of the compensation.
He argues that Ex.BI-Sale transaction dated . 09.02.2004 is in respect of the lands situated i a different village i.e., in Gajulapalli, whereas the acquired lands are situated in Gopavaram Village.
Further, that a small extent of Ac.0.68 cents was sold and the learned Reference Court went wrong in.taking the said transaction into consideration for the purpose of fixing the market value.
He also contends that the value appreciation @ 12% p.a., as adopted by the learned Reference Court ISi not tenable and at the most 10% value appreciation is reasonable.
Making the said submissions, he urges for allowing the appeals.

7. This Court has considered the submissions made and on an  appreciation of the same, the point that arises for consideration is ; Whether r' the Common Order under challenge warrants interference by this Court in the facts and circumstances of the case?
8. At the outset, it may be appropriate to mention that hundreds of acres of land situated in different villages of Nandya'I District were acquired for the purpose of the Telugu Ganga Project.
Most of these villages are contiguous and nature of the land in most of these villages is similar.
Be that as it may.
9. As noted earlier, seeking enhancement of the compensation in respect ' of the subject matter lands, the respondents / claimants got examined R.W.1 (claimant in L.A.O.P.No.820 of 2009) and R.W.2.
They relied on Ex.B1 dated 09.02.2004 which is in respect of land situated ini the neighbouring Gajulapalli Village.

sentences.text: Nothing was elicited in the cross examination contrary to the said version.
On the other hand, R,W.2, who is an attestor of Ex.BI in his cross examination, deposed that the value of the lands of Gopavaram Gajulapalli and Seetharamapuram villages etc., are of the same value.

It was further brought ' on record in the evidence that Gopavaram village is very nearer to Gajulapalli village and the distance between the two villages is 2 Kms., that Gopavaram Village is situated on the main road from Nandyal to Guntur State Highway.
Further, that the lands under acquisition are black cotton soil lands and crops like chillies, jowar etc., are being raised.
No oral evidence was adduced on behaif of the Referring Officer, but as it is cia'im for enhancement, the burden on the respondents to prove their case, by adducing evidence.
The IS evidence brought on record supports their case and no contra evidence was adduced.

Therefore, though Ex.B1-Sale transaction is in respect of another village, taking into consideration the nature of the land potentiality and the distance of 2 Kms., the market value of the subject matter lands can be . determined and the contention of the learned Government Pleader in this regard merits no appreciation.
Fixation of compensation on the basis of the value of the land in the adjoining villages having similar nature and potentiality was approved by the Hon'ble .Supreme Court
in G.M., O.N.G.C. Ltd., v. Sendhabhai Vastram Patel & Ors.,^

10 . Insofar as the other contention advanced by the learned Government Pleader that Ex.B1 is in respect of a small extent and further that value appreciation of 12% p.a., is not tenable / reasonable,
the same deserves no acceptance.

-More than a half acre was sold vide Ex. B1-Sale Deed dated  09.02.2004 which was about one year two months prior to the issuance of Section 4 (1) Notification in respect of the lands in question, it is not the case of the appellant-State that the sale transaction was in respect of some house sites or that the same is not genuine.

Under the said circumstances,
reliance on Ex.BI by the Reference Court cannot be found fault with.
That apart, 12% value appreciation as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Union of India v. Om Prakash (died) by LRs ^ can be taken into consideration.

sentences.text: Therefore, the contentions advanced on behalf of the State are rejected.

The learned Reference Court on a proper appreciation of the matter and keeping in view of the difference between the dry lands and the lands having irrigation source under Category 1 and Category 2 respectively as also by assigning cogent reasons was justified in enhancing the compensation.

This Court, therefore, is of the opinion that the fixation of compensation ii n respect of the subject matter iands is just and reasonable and that there are no good grounds warranting interference by this Court in the order under challenge.
Accordingly, the point is answered.
12. In the aforesaid view of the matter, the appeals fail and the same are accordingly dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, the Miscellaneous .
Applications pending, if any, shall also stand dismissed.
